utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Good morning to everybody in and around the courtroom. Mr. Registrar, please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning, everybody in and around the courtroom. This is case number IT-04-81-T, the Prosecutor versus Momcilo Perisic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Could we have the appearance for the day, please, starting with the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning, Mr. Jevdjevic and everybody in and around the courtroom. Carmela Javier, Barney Thomas, and Salvatore Cannata for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. And for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Good morning to all. Tina Drolec, Gregor Guy-Smith, and Chad Mair on behalf of Mr. Perisic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Just to say, for the record, that we are sitting 15 bis this morning because of an emergency that Judge David has to attend to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Jevdjevic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I hope you have had a good rest last night. Just to warn you that you are still bound by the declaration you made at the beginning of your testimony to tell the truth, the whole truth, and nothing else but the truth.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Mr. Thomas.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Mr. Jevdjevic, I know you've testified for the Defence in the Krstic and Popovic cases. You understand the process that begins now. I represent the Prosecution. I have the opportunity to ask you some questions relating to the testimony that you gave yesterday. Please listen carefully to my questions, answer only my questions, and if you are in any doubt about what I'm asking, please -- or if you don't understand what I'm asking you, please let me know and I will ask you the question another way. All right, are we clear?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Can we please begin with Exhibit P149. If we could have that on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Sir, this was a document that you were asked about yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And if we could just begin with the first page, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: You will see from the first page -- you had not seen this document before yesterday, but you will see from the first page that it is an analysis of the combat readiness and activities of the VRS in 1992. You'll see that that analysis is dated April 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: If we could turn, please, to page 4 in the English and page 5 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: You will see in the top left-hand corner that the analysis has been approved by the commander of the VRS, General Mladic. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: All right. You spoke about several passages relating to radio-relay communications yesterday, and I want to explore that a little further with you, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Could we turn to page 33 in the English and page 31 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Now, sir, do you see the heading "Radio-Relay Communications"?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do. But if possible, could I have a hard copy of this document, because it's very difficult for me to read it on the screen. I can't read it fast enough and efficiently enough. If possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. MAIR
utterances.text: Mr. Thomas that document is in the binder that the witness had yesterday, so --

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Okay. Well, no problem with the binder being provided, and I'm grateful to my learned friend.

utterances.speaker: MR. MAIR
utterances.text: And that will be tab 24.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thanks, Mr. Mair.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And Your Honours, for your assistance, I wish to discuss with the witness or at least draw his attention to the -- the four paragraphs following the heading "Radio-Relay Communications."

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Have you found the -- the page, Mr. Jevdjevic?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Just to yourself, please, can you read -- let's begin with the first three paragraphs. Just read those quietly to yourself for a moment.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Now, I take it, sir, that you -- you do not disagree with what is contained in those three paragraphs in the analysis approved by General Mladic?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I assume that that should be the case, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Okay. Can you read the next paragraph, which begins "The Army of Yugoslavia," to yourself, please.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Okay. Again, sir, I take it you do not disagree with that paragraph?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not disagree with this paragraph. I would like to explain the gist of it, if you allow me.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Well, let me -- I have some questions to ask about the paragraph, sir, so let's deal with my questions first. You will see in the paragraph that there is reference to the Yugoslav Army making available a number of connecting pathways and available capacities of its communication channels at FRY stationary communication hubs. You see that reference?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Particularly, sir, are we talking about the Crni Vrh and Strazbenica hubs?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: I want to deal with each of those one at a time. First, the Cer communication hub -- or "Cer" I think it's properly pronounced. First of all, that is located on the territory of the Republic of Serbia, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And is this communications hub a communications -- a stationary communications node or a stationary communications centre?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's a stationary communications node or hub.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, the second one I mentioned is Crni Vrh. First of all, Crni Vrh refers to the mountain atop which this particular communications hub is positioned; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Both are on top of the mountain.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: We see reference in certain communications charts and communications documentation to a place called Gucevo. Is Gucevo the village or the area, rather, where Crni Vrh is positioned?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The smaller mountain is called Gucevo, and the top of that mountain is called Crni Vrh.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: So where we see Crni Vrh and Gucevo referred to in a communications context, they effectively mean the same thing. We're talking about the same communications hub; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: More or less. It's the same area as far as communications go. At Gucevo there were probably other communications equipment belonging to others, but yes, yes, the reference is the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: All right. And, again, in relation to -- in relation to Crni Vrh, are we talking about a stationary communications node or a centre?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The stationary communications node.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: All right. The third hub that I mentioned was Strazbenica, and can you confirm for us that that is positioned on the territory of Montenegro?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I have been able to follow, we are speaking of two, not three. One is Crni Vrh which is the top of mount Gucevo. That's one and the same thing. And the second is Strazbenica. I don't know what the third one would be.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Okay. I'm moving on now from Cer and Crni Vrh. I want to talk now about the communications hub at Strazbenica. And you will be aware of communications hub at Strazbenica?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And it is hub positioned on the territory of Montenegro?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Again, is this a stationary communications hub or a stationary communications centre?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's a stationary communications hub.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Okay. I want you, please, to look at the next paragraph, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And in the English, Your Honours, we will need to go to the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. MAIR
utterances.text: If I might, the witness had expressed an interest to comment on the paragraph. Mr. Thomas, you said that you would like to ask your questions first, which implied that he might still be allowed to comment. I'm not sure if the witness has done so. I understand I could do it on redirect, but it might be more appropriate to just deal with it while we're on that paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Mr. Jevdjevic, yes, before we leave the paragraph beginning "The Army of Yugoslavia," and in relation to the questions I asked you about that paragraph, is there anything you want to add?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: While you were putting your questions to me, we were talking about the stationary hubs of Crni Vrh and Strazbenica. Later on, you mentioned Cer, which you had not mentioned before. There were three stationary communications hubs on the territory of Serbia by means of which there were transit communication channels that were used, radio-relay communications. The stationary hubs were used for the transit of certain communication channels. They were used when no other connecting pathway was possible in view of optical visibility. That was one of the properties of radio-relay communications I spoke about yesterday. That's why the VRS used this; just as, for example, if you have a plot of land, other users may be allowed passage. So the VRS used the extra capacities or free capacities of the JNA communications so that some of the channels or connecting pathways could pass through those nodes and be reflected as in a mirror back onto the territory of Republika Srpska. That's the way in which these hubs were used. So these were unused capacities that we were able to use. It's like -- it's like having a right-of-way over somebody else's meadow, for example. We didn't have any other way to do this because we needed optical visibility. So those communications would be reflected back onto our side.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: All right. Let me -- let me just discuss that with you for a moment so that I understand what you've said. Depending on the terrain, for example, there might be situations where VRS units could not communicate with each other because there would not be direct optical or uninterrupted optical visibility between two VRS nodes; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And on those occasions, for the VRS units' concern to be able to communicate with each other, are you saying that radio-relay messages would have to be transmitted using the towers also on the territory of the Republic of Serbia and they would ultimately make their way back into the territory of the RS and picked up by the VRS units wanting to retrieve or receive that communication; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And I take it that encryption was used on these -- on the radio-relay routes that passed through the FRY?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Those communications were only transiting, only passing through like a car passing along somebody else's approach road. So it's just transit.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: I -- I understand that, but at the time the message is transmitted by the first VRS unit, it is encrypted; is that right? Or there was that capacity?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The message was encrypted, and it could only be decrypted at its ultimate destination, not while in transit.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: I understand. Within the Drina Corps, there were units who did not have optical line of sight with each other, wasn't there?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: So within the Drina Corps, if a certain unit, for example the Zvornik Brigade, wished to communicate with the Drina Corps command, those radio-relay communications would have to pass through the route that you have described, through Crni Vrh, Cer, and back into the RS, wouldn't it?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Okay. Specifically the Zvornik Brigade -- before we go -- I'm sorry. I'll start again. The main hub in the VRS was Veliki Zep; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Zep, yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And this was a large communications centre on the territory of the Republika Srpska; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: The Drina Corps had a direct -- sorry, the Drina Corps command had a direct link with that communications centre?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: The VRS main -- and before we move from there, the Drina Corps was garrisoned at Vlasenica? The corps command was at Vlasenica?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: We have the VRS Main Staff at Crna Rijeka?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And the VRS Main Staff also had it's own direct link with the communications hub at Zep; is that right? At Zep.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That link was actually by means of an underground table.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Okay. So, for example, for the Drina Corps command to communicate with the Zvornik Brigade, the radio-relay communication would have to go from the Drina Corps command at Vlasenica to Zep, first of all?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Then to the Cer station in Serbia?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Then to the Crni Vrh station in Serbia?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And then back across the border to Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Okay. In respect of other brigades, we had a similar situation where the Strazbenica radio-relay communications centre was used, don't we?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was used for only one brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And which brigade was that?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Rogatica Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: So in that case, communications between the Drina Corps command or the Main Staff of the VRS would be from each of those units, firstly to Zep?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Then through the Strazbenica centre in Montenegro?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And then back across the border to Rogatica?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It's very important to point out that the communications were encrypted in Vlasenica, and no one was able to decrypt it in all these hubs until it arrived at its ultimate destination in the Rogatica Brigade of the VRS. It was only they who could decrypt the telegram, because it only transited through all of these hubs.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: I understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: If you turn over the next page, please, Mr. Registrar, in the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And, Mr. Jevdjevic, if you could go to the next paragraph in the version you have in front of you, you will see a paragraph regarding -- well, you'll see the paragraph. Read it to yourself. "These simultaneous transmission radio-relay communications links ..."

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: I take it you also agree with this paragraph?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: All right. Was it -- excuse me. You've described the encryption of communications travelling across the radio-relay routes that we've described. Was it both oral communication and written communications that was encrypted?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was only written communications that were encrypted, and in part oral communications were also encrypted.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And what would -- okay. All right. Now, we've spoken about this just a little bit, but if we go to the last paragraph before the heading "Radio Communication," which reads "Other units and commands." Do you see that? I think it might be the bottom of your page. Do you see the heading "Radio Communication," sir?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Okay. Have you read the paragraph immediately before that heading?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And, again, do you agree with the comments contained in that paragraph?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As the main communications man in the Drina Corps, on the entire territory of the Drina Corps there were no JNA units before the war, no JNA garrisons, that is, so there was no need to establish stationary communications centres. In my experience, the Drina Corps did not have the possibility of relying on stationary communications centres. In some other corps, and I'm primarily referring to the Banja Luka Corps or the 1st Krajina Corps where there had been many units of the JNA, there were also many stationary communications centres, and probably the chief of the communications who compiled this analysis was referring to those. My experience from the Drina Corps does not correspond to what is stated in this paragraph, but I only knew about one part of all this in relation to the entire VRS.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: All right. Let -- let me deal for a moment with the Drina Corps and your -- your knowledge of operations in the Drina Corps. For combat operations, for example, a forward command post would need to be established; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And was it part of your job to ensure that wherever the forward command post was established that the necessary communications means were also established at that forward command post to enable, firstly, communication back to corps command; and secondly, communication with subordinate units?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And obviously for combat operations as with any military operations, that would include the ability to encrypt information if that was possible?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Okay. Before I talk about the establishment of forward command posts, if the Main Staff of the VRS wished to communicate, say, with Belgrade, so with the General Staff of the VJ, that communication would go through Zep along the same route, through Cer, through Crni Vrh, and on to Belgrade; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MR. MAIR
utterances.text: Before the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Mair.

utterances.speaker: MR. MAIR
utterances.text: Before the witness answers that question, I'm wondering if we could have some foundation for the witness's competence to answer that question regarding the VRS Main Staff and Belgrade. I'm not sure if that has been sufficiently established.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Thomas.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Are you aware, sir, of the radio-relay route from the VRS -- from the RS through to Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I just knew about radio-relay communications that were within the domain of the Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Was there any other radio-relay route from the VRS Main Staff across the border to Serbia other than through Cer and Crni Vrh?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Crni Vrh was only used for the needs of the Drina Corps. I am aware of that and Cer and Strazbenica. I'm not sure about anything else.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: I understand. Let -- just listen to my question for the moment. For the VRS Main Staff to communicate with Belgrade, I mean, I appreciate you can't tell me the entire route because you don't know this, but for the Main Staff in the VRS to communicate with Belgrade, you can at least confirm, can't you, that the communication would have gone from the Main Staff in Crna Rijeka to Zep and then across to Cer?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. MAIR
utterances.text: Again, actually, this time I think Mr. Thomas is asking the witness to speculate, so I will object on those grounds.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Thomas.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: I disagree, Your Honour. The witness has described all the hubs that were applicable from the use of the Drina Corps and the access of the VRS Main Staff to the main RS hub. He's described the radio-relay route across the border into Serbia. All I'm asking him now is that if that would have been the same route that would have been used had communications travelled on from Cer within Serbia. He's someone in a position to answer that question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Notwithstanding his statement that he's not able -- all he knows is communications within the Drina Corps?

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Yes, sir, because all I'm asking him is to confirm that they would have gone to Cer. He says he doesn't know what happened after -- after that, and that's -- that's a matter for him. But I'm only asking him if communications would have gone the same way to Cer and from then on within the FRY by some other means.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Do you here what I'm saying? The witness has indicated that all he knows is the communication within the Drina Corps. He doesn't know any communications outside the Drina Corps. So I don't know whether -- of course, on the other hand, he can say he doesn't know if he doesn't know. If he knows, he knows. I don't know whether you expect him to speculate about what happens outside the Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Well, what he has said, sir, is that the Drina Corps used those Serb facilities. Those Serb facilities were not exclusively for the Drina Corps. He's likened it to somebody driving a vehicle across somebody's property. So what I'm asking him is that if someone wanted to keep driving their vehicle all the way to Belgrade, is that at least the first part of the route that they would have travelled.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The objection will be overruled then.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: So, sir, do you understand my question? You've spoken about multiple users having access to Cer. My question is for a communication from the VRS Main Staff to anywhere in Serbia beyond Cer, would the communication at least have travelled between Zep and Cer?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, we never talked about several users that went to Cer. Whatever I know and whatever is contained in the schematics that I received, it only had to do with the hubs in those of the Drina Corps for the realisation of their own communications. As for the realisation of other communications, I never got any schematics, and I cannot say anything that would be reliable.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can you please listen to the question very carefully and try to answer the question. You're not being asked what you were doing within the Drina Corps. You know -- you've been just asked whether any communication from the VRS Main Staff to anywhere in Serbia beyond Cer would have to go at least through Zep and Cer. The answer to that question is either a Yes, a No, or I don't know; not that long explanation. Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: All right. Can we maybe give you some help.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Can we have P1558 on the screen, please. Now, just before -- just before we blow-up -- excuse me. Just before we blow-up this document, can we see the heading, please, at the top, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Mair.

utterances.speaker: MR. MAIR
utterances.text: I believe the witness also has this document. It might be a little bit easier to see the entire diagram. It should be tab 12, if that's okay with Mr. Thomas.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: That's fine, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Mair.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Now, you see that this is a chart of communications. Do you see the stamp in the middle of that page?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see it, but I cannot read it exactly. I cannot see what is exactly written on this stamp. Maybe -- maybe it says "Main Staff." Now, is it the Army of Republika Srpska or something else? I mean, I have no reason not to trust you. Can you help me out with this?

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Well, have you seen this schematic before or anything --

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Have you seen a --

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: All right. Have you seen a schematic like this before?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Okay. Can we move over to the right-hand side of both versions, please. And in the B/C/S as well, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Now, you'll see the Cer site on that schematic?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Okay. In fact, that's not very clear and it doesn't assist, so we can take that off the screen. My apologies. All right. I want to move now to the establishment of forward command posts, and I want to talk -- so that we have examples that you are familiar with, I want to talk about Srebrenica and Zepa. First of all, you were the -- effectively chief of communications for General Krstic during the Srebrenica and Zepa operations?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Can you explain what role you had during the Srebrenica and Zepa operations?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was an officer from the communications battalion in charge of carrying out the realisation of communications that were planned by Lieutenant-Colonel Nedo Blagojevic who, indeed, was General Krstic's chief of communications.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: All right. And part of your tasks was to ensure the existence of effective and safe communications from the forward command posts; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. To carry out the realisation of communications from the forward command post.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And as you've said before, that would involve ensuring lines of communication from the forward command post back to corps command and also ensuring lines of communication from the forward command post down to subordinate units; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. To realise these communications that you just mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And to ensure, wherever possible, that means existed to encrypt or protect those communications.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: All right. Let's deal with Srebrenica first of all. Where was the forward command post located for the Srebrenica operation?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was in the village of Pribicevac, and that operation was called Krivaja 95. It was not called the Srebrenica operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Okay. In what sort of building was the -- was the forward command post?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Literally in a meadow.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Was there any existing communications capability there before it became the forward command post for the operation?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. Thomas, to interrupt. Sir, when you say literally in a meadow, you mean it was not in a building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Mr. ...

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And in terms of -- first of all, in terms of physically establishing the command post itself, what was involved in that process? I'm not talking about coms for the moment, just the command post itself.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The forward command post in such situations means that there should be a certain area on the ground where elements of the forward command post are deployed. One of these elements of a forward command post is the communications centre, and I was given the task of setting it up.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: I understand, sir. I'm not talking about the communications centre for the moment -- I'm sorry, my friend is on his feet.

utterances.speaker: MR. MAIR
utterances.text: Just briefly, if we could know what "coms" means. I'm not familiar with that term.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Thomas.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: I used the English term "coms," and I apologise. I shouldn't have.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Do you understand that to be a short abbreviation for "communications"?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Now you've confused me. Can you repeat the question?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: It is very difficult to make the distinction in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: I understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: I'll rephrase my question. I'm not talking about communications for the moment. I'm just -- I'm just interested in what physically occurs to establish a command post for all the other elements required to be present at a forward command post. Can you just assist us with describing what is involved in that process?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to regulations, a forward command post would have to imply that there are certain facilities where organs are deployed, organs that are going to command from that forward command post. Security should be deployed there, then the headquarters staff and everyone else that needs to work there for the purposes of that forward command post. That would be it in the briefest possible terms.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Moving now to communications. And for the Srebrenica forward command post, what were you required to do to establish the necessary communications system?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was supposed to establish communications vis-a-vis the superior command, that is to say, the command of the Drina Corps. I also needed to establish communications with subordinate units that took part in the Krivaja 95 operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: So how did you do that?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did that by using certain technical communications.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Without going into too much technical detail, can you describe for us the kind of equipment that you had to establish and how it operated?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On a motor vehicle, I had integrated equipment that made it possible to communicate with the command of the Drina Corps as well as the encryption of these written communications. As for this other type of equipment that had a protection of speech, encryption, rather, I had that kind of equipment for communicating with the subordinate units that took part in the Krivaja 95 operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And did you have encryption capability for the oral communications between corps command and the forward command post?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oral communications between the forward command post of Krivaja 95 and the corps command we could not encrypt. There was only this one device at the Main Staff where from time to time there could be encryption carried out for these oral communications.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: I understand. So that deals with oral communication between the forward command post and the Drina Corps command. What about oral communication between the forward command post and the Main Staff? Was there a direct line of communication between the two?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was not a direct line, but we could get in touch with the Main Staff from that forward command post. However, as far as I can remember, this was used very rarely, because that operation was commanded by the Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, besides encryption, the -- the protection of information also meant that radio call-signs, radio call names, were assigned to certain individuals and to certain posts; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you mean encrypting written communications or oral communications?

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: My fault, sir. I asked you a very long question. For -- for example, for oral communications between the brigade -- or a brigade and corps command or the forward command post, the locations from which people were calling would be identified by call-signs rather than by saying, "I'm calling from corps command," wouldn't they?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We had equipment for the protection of speech, and thereby we could speak openly. There was no need to hide anything orally, no need to code anything when speaking. That is to say, we had reliable radio equipment at short ranges. So from the forward command post through this equipment, one could command the units that took part in the operation by speaking freely, without using any kind of codes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Okay. Nevertheless, there were code-names, weren't there?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the documentation we did have a list of secret names, code-names, for various units, and that is contained in the communications plan. However, all the content of information was enunciated freely, without using any kind of code tables, et cetera. There was no need for that, because our protection equipment was very reliable.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Okay. Before I move on to just a couple of communications I want to talk to you about, can you confirm for me that the code-name for the Drina Corps command during the operation was Zlatar?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Zlatar was the corps command.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: The 1st Zvornik Infantry Brigade was Palma?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was Palma, but I with like to explain something to you if you allow me to do so. These are secret or code-names of units in Zvornik, Vlasenica, Bratunac, et cetera. All these units gave one company or Tactical Group respectively that was singled out from these brigades and went out to carry out the Krivaja 95 operation. These smaller units that left, Palma, Zlatar, and so on, in the execution of Krivaja 95, they were assigned completely different code-names.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: All right. And before we leave this topic, you confirmed that ordinarily Palma meant the Zvornik Brigade and Badem meant the Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: All right. I want to just look at a couple of intercepts where these are used so that you can help us with those, please. The first is P248.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: If we could have that on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: I'll ask you a couple of questions about it, sir, but it might assist you, perhaps, to read the entire transcript in the B/C/S. I'm looking at the one that begins halfway down the page at 2102. Yes. So just take a moment, sir. Read the entire transcript. It's not very long. And we will do the same. And when you need to go on to the -- sorry. When you need to go on to the next page, sir, just say so.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've read it. However, it would be good if I could see a hard copy, because it's hard for me to read it on the screen. However, I have read what is on the screen now.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Take a look at the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: I think, Mr. Registrar, we do need to scroll down in the English. And perhaps once everyone's had an opportunity to read the last part of the English, we can enlarge the B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And when you're ready, sir, we can go back to the beginning of the intercept.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can it be lowered so that I can see the end? I have read as much as it was possible to read.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: All right. If we could go to the beginning of the document, please, or the beginning of the conversation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Mair.

utterances.speaker: MR. MAIR
utterances.text: I am not able to see. I don't know if Mr. Thomas could provide the date for this conversation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Thomas.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: It's the 14th of July, sir, and I was just about to get to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: All right. Mr. Jevdjevic, this is a conversation that occurred on the 14th of July, 1995, and you understand from the date and the contents of this intercept the context. You will see at the reference at the beginning of the conversation we have somebody calling Badem saying that the Palma duty officer wants to talk to Beara. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is what is written here.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: So in the context that we -- that we have been discussing, Palma was the Drina Corps command and Badem refers to the Bratunac Brigade, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Palma, as we said a moment ago, is the command of the Zvornik Brigade in Zvornik, not the command of the Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Sorry, my apologies. The Zvornik Brigade in Zvornik and Badem being the Bratunac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Those are the names of those brigades, the commands of those brigades. However, where their seats are.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: All right. For a communication to be sent from the seat of the Zvornik Brigade to the seat of the Bratunac Brigade, it would have to travel through Crni Vrh, Cer, Zep, and then out to the Bratunac Brigade seat, would it not?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Can we look, please, at P240. And the conversation beginning at 13.58 hours. That's a little further down the page in the B/C/S. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And, Mr. Jevdjevic, I can tell you that this is a conversation from the 16th of July. Again, please just familiarise yourself with the context by reading the intercept or the conversation quietly to yourself.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do apologise, but if we could scroll down so that I can see the beginning and also the right-hand side is cut off, if you want me to look at the content.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: We can do that, sir, and we can go over to the next page for you as well.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've read it, and I assume the content is not that relevant to your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: All right. Well, you haven't heard my question yet. Let's go back to the top of the conversation. You've read the intercept. We know that it's dated the 16th of July, 1995, and you will see that this is a conversation between the Palma duty officer, which we know to be the seat of the Zvornik Brigade, and Zlatar. And Zlatar you described as being the Drina Corps command in Vlasenica. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but I don't see the frequency here, on which frequency this conversation was intercepted, and that is why I cannot tell you what sort of equipment was used, nor can I be sure on which sections this equipment operated. On the previous intercept, I could see the frequency. And that told me something about the type of equipment that was used.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: All right. Well, let me ask you a more -- a general question then. For a radio-relay communication to travel between Zlatar and Palma, it would need to go to, firstly, Zep, then Cer, then Crni Vrh, and then Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Okay. And --

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Although -- I do apologise. I wish to add the following: That was the radio-relay communication used through military equipment exclusively. In the course of the war, we were also able to use civilian telephone lines run by the post office. So every military post had civilian telephone numbers through the post office. So some communications did take place that way. This was the regular military communication line, but we also used civilian ones. Where I can see the frequency of the military equipment, I can say that most likely it went through the route you described. But where I cannot see the frequency, I cannot be certain that this is the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: I understand. I want to move from -- now on to Zepa. I don't have many conversations left to deal with, sir, but I want to move to Zepa, July 1995. Once again, your job was to ensure that there was safe and effective communications capability installed at the various forward command posts; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Can you tell us, first of all, how many forward command posts there were for the Zepa operation?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We moved twice, so we had the 1st, 2nd, and 3rd forward command post.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Okay. I'll just take it slowly so that we have it, sir. Can you tell me, please, where the 1st command post was?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the village of Krivace.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Is -- Krivace is the name of the village?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And in what sort of facility, building, was the forward command post established?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Krivace is a village that was at least 3 or 4 kilometres away from where we were, and the forward command post was underneath a pine tree.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And what communications means were established at that command post?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The same as the one we had for the Krivaja 95 operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: So the same process you described and the same material you described for that operation equally applied to the establishment of this forward command post at Krivace; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but one or two units switched places. Otherwise, everything remained the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: In terms of your communications, the set-up was the same as it was at the Srebrenica forward command post?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Okay. Where was the next forward command post for the Zepa operation?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was called Godjenje.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Prior to the move to Godjenje, what other forward command posts were established for the Zepa operation?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before Godjenje, we had Krivace. After Krivace, we had Godjenje. Maybe I misunderstood your question or it was misinterpreted.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Was there -- all right. Let me be -- let me be a little more specific, sir. Was there a forward command post at Podzeplje?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Or Podplane?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: What was the code-name for the forward command post at Krivace? Was it Uran?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was Uran.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Okay. Within the -- yet you've described that forward command post being under a pine tree. Can you be a little bit more specific? Is there -- for example, does the name Salila mean anything to you?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mesalila means nothing me. I have never heard the word before, or maybe it was misinterpreted. In operations of this kind, our commanders insisted that their forward command posts be at the front line in a place from which one could have an overview over the whole battle-field so that they could see what was going on and thus command the units more effectively. That was why we were on an elevation underneath a pine tree.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: All right. Was there a command post at the post of the 65th Protection Regiment?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That unit was located near Crna Rijeka, but it was not in my line of command, so I do not know where it had its forward command post.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: You weren't aware of that post being at Podplane?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have already told you that this unit was not in the chain of command of the Drina Corps, and I do not know where its forward command post was.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Okay. Let me ask you this: At Uran, you would have encountered General Tolimir during the course of the Zepa operation; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already heard a confusing interpretation again. At Uran I met General Tolimir. Uran was the code-name of the forward command post of the Drina Corps. Can you be more specific?

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Well, was General Tolimir at that command post throughout the Zepa operation?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Was he -- where else was he operating from?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Mair.

utterances.speaker: MR. MAIR
utterances.text: I'm going to object to that question as far as speculation. I don't know if we have any basis at all for Mr. Jevdjevic to answer that question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: How is that speculation, Mr. Mair?

utterances.speaker: MR. MAIR
utterances.text: Well, there's no foundation for how Mr. Jevdjevic would know where Mr. Tolimir was during the Zepa operation. We have no idea where -- where Mr. Tolimir -- we have no idea how Mr. Jevdjevic would have any information at all about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Thomas.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Sir, Mr. Jevdjevic is there. He's in charge of communications. General Tolimir is at the forward command post. He said he's not there all the time. I'm asking him if he knows where else he was operating from.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Objection overruled.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: So, sir, can you -- can you tell us where else General Tolimir was operating from during the Zepa operation?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First, I was never the chief of communications. I was an officer tasked with implementing the communications planned by the chief of communications. General Tolimir was never at the forward command post when Stupcanica 95 was being carried out. But on several occasions I heard General Tolimir's voice on the radio communications, but he never came to the forward command post of the Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Jevdjevic, I want to believe that you do want to go home as soon as possible. Now, that will happen if you can listen to the questions and answer them as succinctly as possible. The question simply is can you tell us where else General Tolimir was operating from during the Zepa operations. You either can tell, or you can't tell. We're not wanting --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't tell you that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. You see, it's a very short answer. Yours was a long answer which will keep you here for the rest of the year. Would that be an appropriate, convenient time? We'll take a break and come back at quarter to 11.00. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Thomas.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Your Honours, there are two documents that I'd like to use with Mr. Jevdjevic for the purposes of impeachment relating to this topic of the existence of other forward command posts at Zepa. The first is an intercept. This is XN222. It is an intercept of a conversation between General Miletic and General Tolimir where General Tolimir has said to Miletic that he has forwarded communication to the Uran command post for the purposes of sending it securely to General Miletic. So the suggestion here that is being made is that Mr. Jevdjevic, at Uran, responsible for communications, would have been aware that General Tolimir was sending him information which was not secure from another location during the operation for the purposes of him -- of him then being able to on-send it securely to General Miletic, suggesting that General Miletic -- sorry, General Tolimir is operating at a location separate from Uran but within the knowledge of Mr. Jevdjevic because he is communicating with Uran, and for the purpose of using the encryption facilities available at Uran for the on-transmission of information. The second document, Your Honours, is used for the same purpose. It's XN220. It is the Drina Corps battle order for the Zepa operation, and it refers to another forward command post. It names it, and I wish to use that document to put to him to establish whether there was another forward command post other than that that he has described.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thanks, Mr. Thomas. Are you done? It's unfortunate that you gave the whole detail of the contents of these documents before you have a ruling on whether you may or may not use them, but let me just find out one thing from the parties. Was Mr. Jevdjevic an operator of the communications systems, or did he just establish them?

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: I think the best answer, sir, is that his evidence was that he was responsible for implementing the communications plan at the forward command posts --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And what does that mean, "implementing the communications plan"?

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Which was to ensure that they were operating, secure and effective communications among all the units.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes. But he's not an operator. He's not the one who answers when people phone.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: He's not been directly asked that question, but there is other evidence that -- that suggests that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Mr. Mair.

utterances.speaker: MR. MAIR
utterances.text: If I could take the second document first, XN220.

utterances.speaker: MR. MAIR
utterances.text: I believe 222 is the first document, if I'm not mistaken.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: My apologies.

utterances.speaker: MR. MAIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, an order that Mr. Thomas spoke about. For 220, if it's only for the purposes of impeachment, we have no problem with that as long as the threshold is met on the subsequent submissions which I assume will be -- will be made. As regards the first, XN222, I don't believe that the submission made thus far by Mr. Thomas actually answers the purpose for which he said he's impeaching the witness. As regards the existence additional communications centres, I don't think there's anything in this intercept that actually establishes additional forward command posts. So I don't think the document itself is actually relevant for the purpose that which Mr. Thomas proposes to use it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. I'm just not finding ...

utterances.speaker: MR. MAIR
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I can assist, I'm referring to Mr. Thomas starting at page 31, lines 10 through 12: "For the purpose of impeachment relating to this topic of the existence of other forward command posts at Zepa."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Mr. Thomas, threshold.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Sir, he's denied that there are other forward command posts at Zepa. I'm just wanting to demonstrate that he's not honest about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Or that he doesn't know. He may not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: He might not know, but he's claimed to say -- that might be his answer, but that wasn't his answer in his testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes. Threshold, Mr. Thomas.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Certainly, sir. The document was disclosed -- sorry, XN220, if I can find my notes -- one moment, Your Honour. XN220 was disclosed on the first occasion on the 13th of October, 2006, and XN222 was disclosed on the 18th of March, this week, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: This week.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Yes, sir. As soon as we received the proofing note effectively from this witness the night before his testimony, we were able to make the necessary inquiries.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: By what means were these documents disclosed?

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: The first via CD, sir, and the second via e-court with a -- with a contemporaneous message saying that it was available in e-court, e-mail message.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Is that all?

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Mair raises the point that the one document is not relevant for purposes of impeachment. Do you have any response to that?

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: I do, sir. The -- the witness has said that there was -- he has no idea where General Tolimir was and what he was doing. It's relevant for the purposes of impeachment in that respect, because it demonstrates that there is a direct communication between General Tolimir, on the 16th of July, and Uran being the forward command post, and I appreciate I need to put him at Uran at the necessary time, but assuming that I do that, he's at Uran, and the communication is for the purpose of transmitting securely information back to General Miletic. So in my submission, it impeaches him on the basis that it challenges his assertion that he didn't know where General Tolimir was or what he was doing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And does that not come back to the question I asked: Was he operating the system or did he just establish the system.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: I can -- understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Obviously if he has -- if he has established the system and he pulls out -- whether he's there or not on the 16th, he's not on the line to hear, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: You're -- no. The -- you're quite right, Your Honour. There are two ways around that. The first is that as a precondition I can ask him some questions as to whether or not he was there on the 16th, but the follow-up conversation in XN222, the Prosecution alleges, is made to him at Uran.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: To him?

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Mair, do you have any comments to make on the document that was first disclosed to you on the 18th of March this year?

utterances.speaker: MR. MAIR
utterances.text: To -- to begin with, I'd like to point out that I think Mr. Thomas has changed the purpose for which he said he would like to impeach Mr. Jevdjevic. He started off by referring to the existence of multiple command posts. We're now dealing with a direct link between Tolimir and Miletic, which is a wholly different topic than with the -- where this conversation started. As regards the submission on the -- the disclosure and the threshold, the Prosecution has tendered hundreds of intercepts in this case, many, many intercepts, and I don't see any reason why this intercept, if it was relevant to this case, why it would not have been tendered at a previous -- previous time or why it was not even disclosed at a previous time sooner than three days ago.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sure, but what -- or is that your objection to the short notice?

utterances.speaker: MR. MAIR
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I don't know whether you want to answer that, Mr. Thomas, or if you don't, then the Chamber will have to rule.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Only to say, sir, that it matters little for our case whether General Tolimir spoke to Mr. Jevdjevic or anyone else on a particular day. It assumes importance now because of the need to impeach Mr. Jevdjevic on his comments regarding where Mr. Tolimir was operating. It's only that the relevance of the document has only now crystallised with this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But then there's a submission by the Defence that you're shifting the goal posts, that you were going to use these documents to impeach him on the number of forward posts, forward command posts. Now you're saying you want to use it to establish the whereabouts of Mr. Tolimir, which is a completely --

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: No -- oh, sorry. The purpose is to impeach his testimony on the whereabouts of General Tolimir. Now, I'm doing that by demonstrating that General Tolimir is there and that he's communicating with others and through him and wanting secure communications and so on, but the purpose has been and always remains to impeach him when he says he doesn't know where General Tolimir was and where he was operating from. Now, if he ends up talking about command posts or about something else, that's by the by. The key thing, sir, is that he has said that he doesn't know where General Tolimir was. General Tolimir would not have been just walking around in fields, sir. He would have been at a command post of some description, but that's not what I'm attempting to establish. The reason why I'm using the document is to impeach his testimony when he says he doesn't know where General Tolimir was during this period.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But let me read you, Mr. Thomas, what you said when you introduced this topic as soon as we came back from the break. And this is at page 31, starting at line 10: "Your Honours, there are two documents that I would like to use with Mr. Jevdjevic for the purposes of impeachment relating to this topic of the existence of other forward command posts at Zepa." That's the point that you want to -- now, when you start talking about the whereabouts of Tolimir, you're shifting from this first purpose, from this first point that you want to impeach him on as to the existence of other forward command posts at Zepa.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Yes, sir, but what I said at line 22 is more specific: "This relates to General Tolimir operating at a location separate from Uran but within the knowledge of Mr. Jevdjevic."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And that's why the Defence is objecting on the basis that that document then is not relevant to the existence of a forward command post at Zepa. It's relevant to the whereabouts of Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Yes, but that's what I've said, sir, at line 22, that General Tolimir is operating at a location separate from Uran but within the knowledge of Mr. Jevdjevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And -- and that separate location, is it a forward command post other than the command posts that he has already mentioned?

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: I don't know. It could be, but it's something within his knowledge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's a fishing expedition, Mr. Thomas.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Sir, he denies knowing where General Tolimir was. He's receiving communications from General Tolimir. He's receiving instructions to encrypt these because he cannot do so from where he's at.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: He's receiving instructions to encrypt.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Yes. The reason why the communication -- the communication between General Tolimir and General Miletic indicates that material is being sent from General Tolimir to Mr. Jevdjevic for the purpose of encryption for on-sending to General Miletic. Now, when Mr. Jevdjevic says he doesn't know where Tolimir was operating from, my submission is that he has to answer that against the document that demonstrates that he's in regular -- in contact with General Tolimir for the purpose of encryption because General Tolimir doesn't have that capability where he is, and so he must know where General Tolimir is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But if -- does that establish where he operates from --

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: I'm not trying to establish by using this document where Tolimir was operating from. I'm impeaching him when he says he doesn't know. The document doesn't tell us where Tolimir was. Now, once I've impeached him, I can go and ask him -- once I put the document to him on impeached him on that point, well, depending what his answers are, I can ask him again where the forward command post --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's my problem. You see, if you depend on what the answers are, that's a fishing expedition, Mr. Thomas. You see, if you impeach, you have incontrovertible information with you which contradicts what the witness is going to say. You're not going to find out still from the witness some information that you may use to impeach.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Except, sir, that if the witness says, "You're right, I did know," then I can ask him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: This is -- you're saying exactly what I'm saying shouldn't happen.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: But --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: If the witness says -- impeachment is not dependent on what the witness is going to say. Impeachment is done on information that is in your possession which is contrary to information that the witness has already given, not which he may give. And then you say "Sir, you said A, B, C, D. Is that correct?" "Yes." "I show you this document. Is that the -- do you know this document?" "Yes." "Is it correct?" "Yes, it is correct." "I'll show you the content. The document says -- contradicts your A, B, C, D. It says X, Y, Z."

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And he agrees with that: "You're right. It says X, Y, Z." And that's meaningless without the next question which is "It was X, Y, Z, wasn't it?" And that's why we would impeach him that way. To get him to agree that it was X, Y, Z.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's right. But it was X, Y, Z not A, B, C, D.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But not on anything that he may say during your questioning. You see, what I hear you saying is for purposes of developing this document that you want to use, you rely on the kind of questions -- answers, rather, he's likely to give as you ask him questions. Now, that is a fishing expedition.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: I hear Your Honour. I can't add any more arguments to what I already have.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Then you can use the one document.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. MAIR
utterances.text: Excuse me. Before we move on, could I just get clarification on the purpose for XN220. Now that we've had this long discussion, I'm a bit confused. If Mr. Thomas could just state the purpose for XN220, the first document -- sorry, excuse me, the second document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: 220 is supposed to demonstrate that, if I may, let me just quote: There are -- to impeach the witness relating to the topic of the existence of other forward command posts at Zepa. As I understand it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MAIR
utterances.text: That is my understanding as well. As long as the document is used for that impeachment and for the sole purpose of impeachment and for no other purpose, then I have no difficulty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Thomas.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: That's how I understood the position, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. You may proceed, Mr. Thomas.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry about that, Mr. Jevdjevic. We thought we must give you a little longer break. I hope you didn't mind that.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Thomas.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Mr. Jevdjevic, there was a question I wanted to ask you about radio-relay stations. As I understand it, for radio-relay messages to be transmitted across a radio-relay route between radio-relay stations, the signal is directional; right? They are sent in a specific direction?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Analogous means that it is not protected, and protected are protected. But both have to be directional. Analogous does not mean directional necessarily.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: All right. I'm sorry, I don't know how analogous got into the question, because it wasn't in my question. For a message to be sent along a radio-relay route, it needs to be transmitted in a specific direction?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And for the radio -- for the communications centre or node receiving the -- the message, the receiver needs to be tuned to the direction from which the signal is coming; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And if either of those are not aligned, you don't have a connection and a break in the route therefore.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: If enemy forces or if anybody wished to disrupt the progress of a signal along a radio-relay route, would that be -- would that be difficult?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that would be difficult for them.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Are the radio-relay routes on the republic of -- or were the radio-relay communication centres on the territory of the RS well protected, well defended?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In what sense do you mean that?

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Well, was there -- was there physical protection? Were there -- were there armed security units there or any other means of military protection? I'm not talking about crypto-protection. I'm talking about actual physical military protection.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those radio-relay nodes that were near enemy positions had their own protection, that is to say, the crew at that node or hub had armed soldiers there.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And presumably that would be to ensure that the communications system was not disrupted? One of the reasons.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, to prevent any kind of sabotage or diversion by the enemy.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Could you disrupt a communication along a radio-relay route simply by changing the alignment of the receivers?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That crew was only supposed to make sure that no one attacks that hub or node.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: I understand. Let's -- let's talk about a situation where we have a communications centre or node with no military protection and an authority has free access to this particular node. Could they disrupt communication along that radio-relay route simply by changing the alignment of the receivers on that node?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Technically that would be possible, but I've never heard of that kind of thing happening during the course of the war in our parts.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Okay. Sir, I want to go back once again to Zepa, and you spoke of the location of the forward command post, which you said was at Krivace.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry. Sorry, Mr. Thomas. Mr. Jevdjevic doesn't get any translation.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Before the interpreter starts interpreting, I hear the Prosecutor speaking at a very high volume, which is stressful.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm sorry about that, Mr. Jevdjevic. Let's see if we can help. Can you try again, Mr. Thomas?

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Can I proceed? Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: You were talking about forward command posts at Zepa. You spoke, first of all, of there being three forward command posts. You said you moved twice and there were three forward command posts for the operation. Can you tell me the location of the three forward command posts?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Krivace, Glodjani, Zlovrh.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And in that order? Was that the order in which they were established?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Could we have document XN220, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Jevdjevic, I'm not certain if you've seen this document before. It is General Krstic's battle order for the operations against Zepa. You will see that immediately above the order numbered 5 on the first page we have reference to the Krivace command post, which you have already spoken about. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: On the next page --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mr. Thomas. I was slow on the uptake. You said immediately before the -- what numbered 5?

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, that's quite correct. We need to scroll down on the English version. I'm sorry. I was reading off a hard copy. Immediately above number 5 we have reference to the Krivace command post.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Command post. Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: On the next page, please, immediately above the number 5, we have reference to another command post, don't we?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please tell me once again which number you want me to look at?

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Above the number 5.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And what is your comment in relation to the reference to this other command post?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the command post of a Tactical Group from the Zvornik Brigade, as far as I can read here, that took part in this operation. That is to say that it is not a command post of the Drina Corps that was actually carrying out this operation where I was. This is a command post of a lower-ranking unit that took part in that operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
