utterances.text: Where was it specifically?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is written here. It says in the village of Podzeplje.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Do you know in what facility?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the village of Podzeplje, but I don't know in what facility. That village was about 3 or 4 kilometres away from my command post.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Did you go there?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Did you have communications with them?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: What -- did you have secure communications with them?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Were there other command posts for other units involved in Zepa other than this one?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The order specifies the initial command posts for all the units involved, and that's the way it goes down the chain vertically.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: My question was: Were there other command posts for other units?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course. Of course. Of course. All units received their command posts through an order.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Can you tell me -- tell us, please, where the other command posts were?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can tell you, for instance, if I read this order. However, my duty was only to know where my command posts were.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, but do you know where other command posts were? If you don't know, you don't know.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Maybe at that point in time I did know roughly, but all of that is nearby. I can communicate with everyone, so it didn't really matter to me that much. Probably I did know approximately.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Do you know now? Can you remember any now?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no. No, no. I just remember the ones where I was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Thomas.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: All right, Mr. Jevdjevic. I've nearly finished. I've just got a couple of questions that I want to ask you about your service, please. First of all, you applied for and got double years of service for your pension from the VJ in respect of the time you spent serving in the VRS specifically from up until March 1996; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please repeat that, because I seem to be hearing both you and the interpreter at the same time, so I didn't quite understand what you were saying.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Okay. You receive a military pension?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: It covers your entire period of service in the JNA, the 30th Personnel Centre, VRS, and the VJ, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: In respect of the years you spent in the VRS while the war was occurring in Bosnia, you received double years' service for your pension; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: All right. From the period 1 September 1994 until the 31st of January, 1995, we have heard evidence that the money for -- or salaries stopped getting paid for members of the 30th Personnel Centre. Was your salary stopped during that period?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And did you successfully apply for the payment of that salary in -- many years later, in 2001?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There was a procedure before the organs in charge in Serbia. I personally did not ask for that, but that was resolved in a uniformed manner for all.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Could all other microphones please be switched off when the witness is speaking. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: My apologies, Madam Interpreter.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: You spoke yesterday, Mr. Jevdjevic, of your training in the VJ, specifically you said that you were serving in the VRS until you were sent for a year's training in the VJ, whereupon you returned to the VRS, which is where you spent your time until you retired. You recall giving that testimony yesterday?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: You were transferred to the military school on the 9th of June, 1998. Does that sound right, sir?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably, if there is information to that effect. I don't remember it exactly, but probably it was then, 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And you were returned by order of the chief of personnel of the General Staff of the VJ to the 30th Personnel Centre on the 2nd of August, 1999. Does that sound right, sir?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Mair.

utterances.speaker: MR. MAIR
utterances.text: It appears that Mr. Thomas is reading from a document, and the witness seems a bit unclear. I don't know if it would be beneficial for the witness to view the document. That might clarify some of this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Thomas.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: That won't be necessary, sir. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: So you were transferred back to the 30th Personnel Centre August 1999. Does that sound correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I was returned to the VRS because I was its member, but this paperwork was never available to me, and I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Well, here's something you might know, sir. Can you explain to Their Honours why you didn't tell them that you served in Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nobody asked me that.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: You were asked to summarise your military service after 1995.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nobody asked me that. I can always say that. I have no problem in saying that.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Well, you didn't say that yesterday. But, nevertheless, you acknowledge you served in Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: During my schooling, the aggression against Serbia occurred. We were all there in that academy, the school centre where we had been reassigned, and then we were all assigned to certain war units, and I have no reservations in saying that to anyone, any time, anywhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Except --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Jevdjevic, I will ask you one more time. Please listen to the question and answer the question. The question simply is: But nevertheless, you acknowledge you served in Kosovo? Your answer is going to either be a Yes or a No. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That way, you'll go home quicker.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Mr. Jevdjevic, I just want to see that I have certain things straight. And as it -- through the Bosnian war you were fighting as a member of the VRS; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: You had your status regulated through the 30th Personnel Centre?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: You were transferred to the military academy in 1998?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: The military academy was in Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: While you were at the military academy, you were deployed to Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That was our own choice.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: You were ordered there by order of the chief of the personnel administration of the General Staff of the VJ, assigned to the VJ 3rd Army.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Some of us did not respond to that call, others did. Those who did not went back to the VRS, and those who did were redeployed to the 3rd Army.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And after service in Kosovo, you returned and were deployed back to the VRS. Is that your position?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I came back, completed my schooling, and after completing my schooling I returned to the army of the VRS.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: All right. Mr. Jevdjevic, thank you. That concludes my questions for you.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Thomas. Mr. Mair, any re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. MAIR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. If I could just have one moment. I think it would go much quicker if I could have that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MAIR
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MAIR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I have just a few questions. Thank you for the moment. I think this will be rather short, I hope.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Mair.

utterances.speaker: MR. MAIR
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Jevdjevic.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. MAIR
utterances.text: If we could just pick up the -- the topic you were just discussing with Mr. Thomas regarding your time at the school in Belgrade and Kosovo. Do you recall how many members of the VRS attended this school at the same time as you?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There were 32 of us.

utterances.speaker: MR. MAIR
utterances.text: And at page 50, line 12, starting at line 12, you said: "Some of us did not respond to that call, others did." Could you tell us how many responded to that call?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thirty of us.

utterances.speaker: MR. MAIR
utterances.text: The 30 of you who responded to the call, did they all go to the same place?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We were deployed all over the war theatre of Serbia and Montenegro. I happened to be assigned to the garrison at Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. MAIR
utterances.text: Who was the Chief of Staff of the VJ when you were deployed to Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MAIR
utterances.text: Very well. I just have one other topic. During your testimony with Mr. Thomas, you discussed --

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do apologise. I think it was General Ojdanic. I think it was General Ojdanic. And General Pavkovic was the commander of the 3rd Army.

utterances.speaker: MR. MAIR
utterances.text: Okay. During your testimony with Mr. Thomas you were asked a series of questions about Pribicevac, the forward command post during the Krivaja 95 operation. Do you recall that testimony?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MAIR
utterances.text: How long were you at the forward command post at Pribicevac? Until what date?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Until the 11th of July, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. MAIR
utterances.text: A that point, on the 11th of July, where did you go?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I disbanded the communications centre for commanding that operation. And acting on the personal orders of General Mladic, I was transferred to establish the communications centre for the Stupcanica operation in the general area of Zepa.

utterances.speaker: MR. MAIR
utterances.text: When you say that you disbanded the communications centre, what do you mean? What was the -- what did you actually do?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I set up a new communications centre to serve the needs of the command post for the operation at Zepa.

utterances.speaker: MR. MAIR
utterances.text: Regarding the disbanding of the old command post, what sort of communications were left in the area, if anything? And by "the area," I'm referring to Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honours. I don't see how that arises, that question arises out of cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Mair.

utterances.speaker: MR. MAIR
utterances.text: Your Honour, without getting too deeply into it, we've dealt with the communications at both Srebrenica and Zepa, as well as several intercepts at that point in time, and so the question is relevant as to the existence of the communications system and conversations that took place in that time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm not quite sure I understand what you are saying, Mr. Mair. You know, the -- do -- how is it relevant to the existence the communications system and conversations? Are you going to tell us all about the conversations that took place? I'm not quite sure what you're saying.

utterances.speaker: MR. MAIR
utterances.text: I certainly hope not. No. We've -- Mr. Thomas showed Mr. Jevdjevic several intercepts that took place during the 14th and the 16th of July and a little bit later. Mr. Jevdjevic just discussed that on the 11th of July he disbanded the forward command post. I am simply trying to see what the effect of that was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Given that the intercepts that were given are after the 11th -- are dated after the 11th?

utterances.speaker: MR. MAIR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. The objection is overruled, and I will allow the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MAIR
utterances.text: Mr. Jevdjevic, I will repeat my question: "Regarding the disbanding -- the disbanding of the old command post, what sort of communications were left in the area, if anything, and by "the area," I'm referring to Srebrenica."

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No communications were left. When the communications centre is disbanded, there's no longer any possibility of commanding the units that had participated in that operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MAIR
utterances.text: Mr. Jevdjevic, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. MAIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much, Mr. Mair. Judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Jevdjevic, I would like to ask you one or two questions regarding the transmission, the communications system of the VRS. You told us that almost all transmissions or communications went through Serbia and Montenegro; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The army of VRS used stationary hubs at Crni Vrh, Cer, and Strazbenica, which were in the immediate vicinity of the border with Serbia. These were the end points used to reflect certain communications back to our own side. The VRS had its independent communications system, and only the Drina Corps at the far east, in order to communicate with certain of its brigades, had to carry out transit through points on several hills which are actually very close to the border with Serbia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just to be sure I understand correctly, so you're talking about relays. Those relays which were allowing communications to go through the Drina Corps army did not go through Serbia and Montenegro? Is that what you're saying? I thought that this is what you said during your testimony, but now I'm a little lost.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The VRS had a completely autonomous communication system, completely independent. Only at its eastern end, where the Drina Corps was, near the River Drina, because of the lack of optical line of sight with certain units we used three relays on the territory of Serbia and Montenegro which we used only for purposes of transit of communications for the needs of the Drina Corps of the VRS.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you very much. This is what I thought you said earlier. But now regarding the communications, they were all encrypted; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All written communications were encrypted, but only some oral communications were encrypted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Was the VJ able to know what written communications said? Were they able to decode those communications? Were they able to get the codes?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No. Our units had the codes according to its level, the level of the unit. So only units having corresponding code books could decrypt each other's messages, and this was all organised by unit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But in every army you have specialised services, specialised in decoding transmissions. It's a classic case; right?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I'm being very practical in my explanations. To avoid having certain levels of command bypassing their immediate superiors, the brigade had one code book which was valid as far as the corps command, and it was only on that stretch that they could encode and encrypt and decrypt. And then further on another code would be used. So only at the two end points could the messages be decrypted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. But according to you, the Yugoslav Army did not have the necessary codes to decode these transmissions or these communications?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I really don't know that. I don't know. I only know as far as the Drina Corps level is concern. So I really couldn't answer your question. What we encrypted at the level of the Drina Corps and within the VRS as an independent communication system, I'm sure the VRS did not have those code books. I'm absolutely sure of that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You mean the VJ, not the VRS?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Yes. The VJ was independent and autonomous, as was the VRS. And no one, including the VJ, could decode messages sent by the VRS.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's theoretically the case, but in practice there were many VJ officers such as you who were in the VRS. That allowed, in a certain way, for codes to be given to the Yugoslav Army; right?

utterances.speaker: MR. MAIR
utterances.text: Excuse me. I don't mean to interrupt, but just so I can understand. "There are many VJ officers such as you." I don't know that we've had evidence of that. I just want to make sure that was not a translation issue, that's all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Is that a question for me?

utterances.speaker: MR. MAIR
utterances.text: Yes, it was, Your Honour. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's what I said, in fact, that there were VJ officers who worked in the VRS, just like our witness today, and this is why I wanted to know. He was, if I understood correctly, a VJ officer before working for the VRS. He was still paid by the VJ. And then afterwards he was trained at the VJ academy. He was first -- well, he was in the VJ when he went to Kosovo. Maybe I sort of shortened the question or put it all together, but that was, in fact, my question.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You've put several questions. I personally felt, and I still feel that way, as a member of the VRS. I was sent for schooling to Serbia following an order of the VRS. And if anything urgent happened, I would immediately be sent back. But now I'll answer your question. As regards encryption --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm interrupting you only to tell you the following: What you're saying is not exactly true. It's not the VRS who sent you to Kosovo; right?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When the VRS sent us for schooling, we entered the chain of command of the school, and all my colleagues who were in Greece at the academy and a colleague of mine who was in a French school in Saint Cyr, they all became part of that chain of command of -- of the school or academy where they were. We shared the same schoolrooms, the same facilities --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to stop you here because that was not my question, and I would not like to go into this to know whether some Yugoslav officers who were on training ... but that was not my question. My question was the following: I wanted to know if, by the fact that there were many VJ officers in the VRS, if that did not contribute, was this not an important factor in the sense that the communications could be decoded by the VJ? There were means. It was easy to just share codes or to give codes. Maybe for you it was not really important that the VJ made decode your transit communications; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In -- to be involved in encryption involves the highest confidentiality, the highest state secret. I did not complete the course for encryption because I failed to fulfil some security conditions. I'm just saying this to show how strict these conditions were and how important it was for all those involved in encryption to observe the strictest confidentiality. I never heard of anyone involved in encryption selling or lending or giving anybody else the code books.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you very much for your answers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Any questions arising from the questions by the Bench, Mr. Mair?

utterances.speaker: MR. MAIR
utterances.text: Just briefly, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MAIR
utterances.text: Just so that we're clear, Mr. Jevdjevic, you were not a VJ officer at any point in time; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: During the war from 1992 onwards, from the point of time when the VRS was established, I was always a member of the VRS.

utterances.speaker: MR. MAIR
utterances.text: Thank -- one second, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MAIR
utterances.text: I have nothing further, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Mr. Thomas? Thank you so much. Mr. Jevdjevic, that brings us to the end of your testimony. Thank you so much for coming to testify at the Tribunal, and may you travel well back home. You are now excused. You may stand down. Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. That concludes the witnesses that we have for the balance of today. Our next witness is scheduled for Monday morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Have you finished? She wanted to tell you something before you sit down.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I better make sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I'm okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Then we stand adjourned to Monday morning at 9.00, Courtroom II. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 22nd day of March, 2010, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 11.58 a.m.,
